item.content:encoded:
Czech municipal and Senate elections: a warning for the governing coalition

发布源: 19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland | 抓取时间: 2026-10-21

A week-long series of elections to the Czech Senate (the upper house) and local councils concluded on 17 October. One-third of the Senate is elected every two years for a term of six years. Of the 27 seats contested, the liberal Mayors and Independents (STAN) won 10, followed by the right-wing Civic Democratic Party (ODS) with seven. The ODS will therefore retain the largest parliamentary group in the Senate, formed jointly with the liberal TOP 09 party, as well as the Senate presidency. All three parties are in opposition in the Chamber of Deputies (the lower house). Meanwhile, the governing coalition’s parties failed to win a single seat.

In the municipal elections held on 9–10 October, Prime Minister Andrej Babiš’s ANO received the most votes,but performed worse than in 2022. Its share of the vote fell from 16.6% to 14.3%, while the number of councillors elected dropped from 1,748 to 1,650. ANO came first in six of the 13 regional capitals, including Ostrava, but its support declined in 12 of them, with Plzeň being the only exception. A change of mayor is also likely in Prague, where STAN won the election and is best placed to secure the post. The new city council is expected to elect STAN’s lead candidate in Prague, Petr Hlaváček, to replace Bohuslav Svoboda of the ODS. In smaller municipalities, independent candidates once again dominated, winning more than 81% of the seats.

Published: October 7, 2026

On 22nd September, in her speech at the United Nations General Assembly (UN GA) the Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi - as the first Japanese leader since 2005 - urged the removal of the ‘enemy state’ clause from the UN Charter. The provision was included in the UN's founding document to denote nations that fought against the Charter’s original signatories during World War II, specifically targeting Axis powers such as Germany, Italy and Japan. Although over eight decades have passed since the end of the conflict and the ‘enemy states’ are well-functioning democracies, the clause remains in its original form. Moreover, in 1995 the UN GA adopted a resolution stipulating it had ‘become obsolete’ and called for its erasure from the Charter.

Published: October 7, 2026

According to Finnish media reports, the United Kingdom has proposed extending a nuclear umbrella over the members of the Joint Expeditionary Force (JEF). Apart from France and the United States, the UK is the only NATO member possessing its own nuclear capability. The initiative arose in response to declining faith in the nuclear umbrella provided by the United States. Poland's participation in the format would make sense if it were covered by the initiative's nuclear deterrence.

item.content:encoded:
A unilateral ‘energy truce’? Day 1693 of the war

发布源: 19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland | 抓取时间: 2026-10-21

Despite a slowdown in the pace of Ukrainian counterattacks in the Lyman sector, the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) are not giving up on their attempts to dislodge the enemy from most of the remaining positions on the western bank of the Zherebets River.Ukrainian troops have managed to expand the area under their control in the northern part of Zarichne and advance towards the town centre. The defenders have also managed to regain control of most of the large forest complex north of Rai-Oleksandrivka. Fighting for its central streets is currently taking place, though a vast grey zone still persists there. According to unconfirmed reports from Russian sources, the Ukrainians have managed to cross the Donets–Donbas Canal in small groups.

Fierce fighting is ongoing in the Dobropillia area, where Russian forces are attempting to penetrate from the south into the town centre in small groups.Ukraine, meanwhile, is attempting to counterattack north of the town, consolidating their positions in Zolotyi Kolodiaz and preventing the Druzhkivka conurbation from being encircled from the west. Russia is continuing its infiltration ofOleksiievo-Druzhkivka, though fierce fighting is still ongoing in the vast grey zone in the north-western part of Kostiantynivka.

item.content:encoded:
Defence and International Security

发布源: 36. Casimir Pulaski Foundation --Poland | 抓取时间: 2026-10-21

The Pulaski Foundation Defence and Security Program provides multidisciplinary analysis of the current and emerging defense and security challenges facing the Transatlantic Alliance – with a special focus on Central and Eastern Europe.

Since 2022 the program allocates much of its resources to analysing the possible outcomes and consequences for European security of the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine. A special component of the program is devoted to the challenges and opportunities facing Poland’s defense policy, including modernizing of the Polish army and its industry. The main goal is to present actionable recommendations to an array of Polish stakeholders, including public administration, which could form a basis for long-term strategies for Poland in times of raising military and defense demands.

Overall, through its analysis, the program advocates for a stronger presence of NATO on the Alliance’s Eastern Flank, more developed European defence capabilities and argues for the need to provide military assistance and solid security guarantees to Ukraine.
